meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start, but I have a client call at 4:40. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
A forty-minute piece in class against an essay he wrote over a weekend, with books open. You didn't answer me, Hale: who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay, the checker is off the table, and I'm writing that down. What version history, Hale? Show me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed that the AI checker proves nothing by itself and said you were taking it off the table. I still require the zero withdrawn, an answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard before it was entered, and a copy of the version history you referred to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard first, and to see the version history.
What moved her: "I'm taking it off the table" earned a flat okay and a note on her pad, because dropping the detector score removed the thing she trusts least.
What cost ground: "I want to be fair to Owen" opened with a claim of fairness while her question about who decided went unanswered twice, and the September 24 comparison let her set a timed class piece against a weekend essay.
Try next time: in your first reply, own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then put the dated version history in front of her before you mention the September 24 writing.
